newsitem.title: USA: More insurance broker takeovers now less likely.
newsitem.headline: More insurance broker takeovers now less likely.

text.p: The global insurance brokerage industry may not see any more big takeover deals in the near future now that Aon Corp has agreed to buy Alexander & Alexander Services Inc, analysts said.
Merger speculation has been rife over the past few months as the insurance brokers struggled to cope with declining revenues amid soft insurance pricing.
Although most insurance brokers were seen as potential takeover candidates, Aon was considered the only likely buyer, analysts said.

But Aon is not likely to make any more major acquisitions in the near-term after its agreement to purchase Alexander & Alexander for $1.23 billion and a previously announced acquisition of Bain Hogg Group from Inchcape Plc for 160 million stg cash.
"It does mop up a lot of the capital that was in theory available to invest in the brokerage business," said Conning & Co analyst Gary Ransom.
"The one obvious buyer is now less obvious," he said.
Other rumored takeover targets have included Sedgwick Group Plc and Willis Corroon Group Plc.
In August, Sedgwick chief executive Sax Riley said the company would consider a merger with another broker if the proposal fitted its strategy.
St. Paul Cos Inc, meanwhile, earlier this year put its Minet brokerage up for sale.
Longer-term, after it digests these acquisitions, Aon still might return to the merger market, Ransom said, noting that Aon has other life insurance assets it could sell to raise capital for deals.
However, pressure to cut costs could encourage other brokers to negotiate deals in the meantime, analysts said.
"One of the main reasons Aon is doing this is to reduce its cost structure," Alan Levin, managing director of Standard & Poor's insurance rating services said.
To the extent Aon can reduce its cost structure, it will become an even more formidable competitor than it already is, he said.
"There's already been significant acquisitions and mergers in that business. May there be more - perhaps," he said.
"There's internal needs for brokers to gain some control over their cost structure and this will just ratchet up the pressure a little bit, Levin said.
But Aon's deal with Alexander & Alexander is not likely to prompt Marsh & McLennan Cos Inc to respond with any special action, Salomon analyst Michael Smith said.
The consolidation, however, could have a positive effect by decreasing some of the competitive pressure on pricing, he said.
"The consolidation lessens the competition a little bit," Smith said.
And the Alexander & Alexander takeover may disrupt its relationships with some of its clients, providing competitors with some potential for new business, Ransom said.
"In the long run, it's probably good. You needed consolidation of this business," Ransom said.
